frameworks.name: Value Equation Framework
frameworks.definition: A four-component model defining value as dream outcome minus time delay, effort burden, and probability of success.

claims.text: Value is determined by what people willingly pay for; if a customer pays you for something, they have found value in it.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: The value equation has four components: dream outcome (the ultimate goal), time delay (how long it takes), effort/burden (what the customer must sacrifice), and probability of success (likelihood of achieving the outcome even with full compliance).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

anchors.value: sacrifices customer must make (action and inaction)
likelihood of success despite all sacrifices

claims.text: Personal training (fitness service) is lower-value because achieving a six-pack takes two years of daily effort, requires stopping enjoyable behaviors (weekend drinking, eating tacos), and carries execution risk of failure despite full compliance due to genetic factors.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Lower value perception = (long time delay) + (high daily effort) + (prohibited enjoyable behaviors) + (success risk from genetics). Customers must spend hours arguing/negotiating during sales because the value proposition requires extensive justification.
bounded_by: Specific to personal training fitness offerings

claims.text: GLP-1 pharmaceuticals (combined with muscle-preserving drugs) are higher-value than personal training because they deliver the same dream outcome (improved physique) with no time delay, virtually no willpower or effort, and near-guaranteed success regardless of genetics.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Higher value perception = (fast result) + (zero willpower required) + (virtually guaranteed success) + (genetic-proof). The reduced friction dramatically simplifies the sales process because customers perceive immediate, reliable value.
bounded_by: Assumes customer comfort with pharmaceutical intervention

claims.text: Fundamentally, differentiation of value is accomplished by restructuring the value equation—reducing time delay, cutting effort/burden, increasing probability of success, or clarifying the dream outcome—rather than promoting a better version of the same burden structure.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Superior offers solve the four variables of the value equation more elegantly than inferior offers. Competitors offering the same burden structure cannot differentiate unless they reframe which variable they optimize.

examples.text: A prospect evaluates fitness transformation: personal training promises a six-pack physique (dream outcome) but requires two years of daily gym sessions (time delay), stopping alcohol and tacos (behavior change burden), muscle soreness, tiredness, and the risk that poor genetics prevent the result despite full effort (probability of success risk). The combined burden makes closing the sale require extended negotiation (roughly an hour of persuasion per client). The same prospect evaluates GLP-1 plus muscle-preserving drugs: same physique result (dream outcome) but takes no time (fast), requires only medication compliance (no willpower), and works regardless of genetics (virtually guaranteed). The pharmaceutical path sells easier because value is compressed into fewer friction points.

practices.text: When selling a service, map the four-component value equation explicitly for your offer and identify which variable (time, effort, success probability, outcome clarity) is your competitive weakness relative to alternatives. Optimize that variable first to increase perceived value and reduce sales friction.
